newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ CTU urges exporters to avoid simplistic answers.
newsitem.headline: NZ CTU urges exporters to avoid simplistic answers.

text.p: An exporters' economic summit on Thursday must avoid "simplistic" solutions to exporters' problems, the Council of Trade Unions (CTU) said on Wednesday.

The CTU, which was not invited to the meeting, said it had sent the summit a paper urging it to avoid simplistic solutions such as advocating cuts in government spending or further reductions in wages.
The CTU said exporters and those competing with imports were in an economic gridlock, as they were trapped under the burden of high interest and exchange rates.

This forced producers to cut back on borrowing for capital development, and on spending on productivity-enhancing activities such as training and research. The CTU said a slowdown in the growth of capital per worker showed up in lower labour productivity, which forced monetary authorities to keep the exchange rate high to keep inflation under control.
"The end result is that keeping inflation inside a narrow '0 to 2 percent' band, at a time when labour productivity growth is negative, imposes impossibly severe operating conditions on exporters."
The CTU said cuts in government spending were not a solution because excessive government spending was not the problem.
"There is a negative public sector borrowing requirement, so excessive spending cannot be a cause of high interest and exchange rates," the CTU said.
It advocated a two-part approach to exporters' problems -- easing monetary settings and adopting a broader approach to raising productivity.

Improving the capital intensity of production, level of skills used and the productivity of labour all required a rebuilding of the infrastructure, improved training and the development of a coherent industry policy.

"An active partnership between the government and exporters for sustainable development is the only option left after the devastation caused by the experiment with monetarist disinflation," the CTU said.
